author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Reduce distant texture shimmer without blurring the PS2 image
summary: Build a repeatable camera route across roads, fences, or terrain, test mipmapping before anisotropic filtering, compare native and target resolution, and accept only a setting that stabilizes detail in motion.
heroAlt: PCSX2 native-resolution sampling diagram used to explain texture behavior during upscaling

blocks.text: Use motion to expose unstable texture detail

Shimmer is a temporal problem: fine texture patterns switch rapidly as the camera moves because distant texels are sampled inconsistently. A still image may look sharp while the route sparkles in play. Choose a straight road, tiled floor, wire fence, or terrain slope with controllable camera speed. The route must be long enough to see distance transitions and short enough to repeat with the same inputs.
Do not start by forcing the highest anisotropic level and a sharpening shader together. Either can change apparent detail without proving whether the title's mip levels are being selected correctly.

items: An in-game save before a ten-to-twenty-second camera movement.
Native-resolution and target-resolution recordings of the unchanged route.
Default texture filtering and automatic hardware mipmapping recorded.
Post-sharpening, texture replacement, and display enhancement disabled.
A foreground UI element in view to detect unwanted global blur.

blocks.text: Test mip selection before oblique filtering

items: 1. Run the route at native resolution and mark where distant detail begins to flicker.
2. Repeat at the intended upscale multiplier without changing filtering or renderer.
3. If shimmer grows with resolution, return to native and test the next supported mipmapping accuracy level.
4. Record the same route and compare transitions rather than individual sharp frames.
5. Once mip transitions are stable, test moderate anisotropic filtering on surfaces viewed at a steep angle.
6. Inspect fonts, sprites, and texture-atlas edges for halos, seams, or unexpected softening.
7. Move back to the target resolution and repeat after the device reaches normal operating temperature.
8. Store mipmapping and filtering only in the affected title profile if a second game regresses.

blocks.text: Mipmaps provide smaller prefiltered texture levels for distant surfaces, while anisotropic filtering improves samples viewed at oblique angles. They solve related but different sampling problems. Upscaling can reveal gaps and atlas assumptions that were hidden at the PS2's sampling rate, so a sharper output is not automatically a more stable or faithful one.
Judge the full route at normal playback speed and then inspect representative frames.

items: Distant patterns change smoothly instead of sparkling between frames.
Roads and floors remain detailed at oblique angles without crawling edges.
HUD text and 2D sprites keep their intended sharpness.
Texture-atlas borders do not bleed into adjacent artwork.
The chosen combination has no sustained thermal or frame-time penalty.
Shimmer decreases only because the entire frame is blurred: restore the previous filter.
New colored seams appear around sprites: remove forced filtering and retest the atlas.
Only one upscale multiplier fails: keep the last stable resolution instead of stacking corrections.
Surface flicker remains in software at native output: confirm whether the original game behaves the same.

blocks.text: Return sampling controls to game-safe values

Restore automatic mipmapping, game-controlled texture filtering, and the prior internal resolution. Disable any sharpening stage introduced during comparison, cold-boot the saved route, and confirm the baseline shimmer pattern before attempting a documented title-specific fix.
Video compression hides and invents shimmer

Low-bitrate recordings can turn fine detail into blocks or smooth away temporal crawling. Keep local high-quality captures for analysis and treat streamed versions only as navigation aids, not as final evidence.
